q: The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by Oersted in 1820.
e: Oersted is credited with discovering the magnetic effect of electric current in 1820.

q: When a straight wire carrying a current is placed above a compass needle, the needle is deflected.
e: This deflection was the key observation in Oersted's experiment.

q: The deflection of a compass needle near a current-carrying wire is due to a magnetic force acting on it.
e: The current produces a magnetic field, which exerts a magnetic force on the compass needle.

q: The direction of the magnetic field due to the current flowing through a wire can be found by using the right-hand rule.
e: The right-hand rule is the standard method for determining the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.

q: In the right-hand rule, if the thumb points along the wire in the direction of the current, the direction of the fingers will give the direction of the magnetic field.
e: This is the correct application of the right-hand grip rule.

q: The magnetic lines of force around a wire carrying a current are closed circular loops in the plane perpendicular to the wire.
e: This accurately describes the geometry of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire.

q: If the current flowing through the wire is reversed, the direction of the magnetic field will remain the same.
e: If the current flowing through the wire is reversed, the direction of the magnetic field will also be reversed.

q: A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire, which has a magnetic field inside and in its vicinity when a current flows through it.
e: This is the definition of a solenoid and its magnetic property.

q: The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a bar magnet.
e: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field pattern similar to a bar magnet.

q: When viewing one end of a solenoid, that end will be a south pole if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction.
e: This is the correct rule for determining the polarity of a solenoid.

q: When viewing one end of a solenoid, that end will be a north pole if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction.
e: This is the correct rule for determining the north pole of a solenoid.

q: According to Fleming's left-hand rule, if the first finger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the second finger in the direction of the electric current, the thumb will point in the direction of the motion along which the force acts.
e: This is the correct statement of Fleming's left-hand rule for motors.

q: When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field, it experiences a force that is perpendicular to both the magnetic field $B$ and the velocity $v$.
e: The magnetic force on a moving charge is always perpendicular to both the field and the velocity vector.

q: If the particle moving in a magnetic field is a negatively charged one, the force acting on that particle will be in the opposite direction.
e: The direction of force on a negative charge is opposite to that on a positive charge under the same conditions.
